graph.name: Riot Games Data Ingestion Architecture
graph.notes: Architecture for global telemetry and player data ingestion for League of Legends, reducing data availability latency from 6-24 hours down to 5 minutes.

nodes.name: User
nodes.notes: Game clients connecting across 20+ shards worldwide.

nodes.name: EKS
nodes.notes: Runs API receiving player experience telemetry from game clients.

nodes.name: OnPremDC
nodes.notes: On-premise game servers buffering data in local Kafka before replication.

nodes.name: MSK
nodes.notes: Regional managed Kafka streaming buffer handling up to 500,000 events per second.

nodes.name: S3
nodes.notes: Central data lake storing ~8 TB per day in Delta Lake format via Spark streaming.

nodes.name: GLUE
nodes.notes: Data catalog/metastore and permission/access management layer for analysts and engineers.

edges.notes: Game client sends API requests and telemetry to EKS.
Players connect to regional game servers.
EKS forwards collected data to MSK regional buffer.
Local Kafka buffers data and uses MirrorMaker to replicate into regional MSK clusters.
Spark streaming job writes data from MSK to Delta Lake on S3.
